title: Onkyō Atlas

text.mapBlurb: The in-game map app's own tiles, drawn from the plan. Drag, pinch, scroll to zoom; pins are the places built so far.
text.placesBlurb: Set pieces and rooms as they are built, graybox and all. Renders are the kits' own review shots.
text.kitBlurb: Four kits, all data in and geometry out. City facts live in the city's files; the code knows nothing about Onkyō.
text.footer: Rendered from one plan file by CityKit's kits. Coordinates are plan metres: +x east, +y north, the conservatory at the origin.

tagline: A city built from one plan file, and the set pieces the game is played in.

name.gloss: The music college on Jōon hill.

places.blurb: Jōon College of Music on its hill: the game's hub. The old brick hall with a working fly tower, a trap room and a revolve; the practice wing; the lecture wing; the production block.

name.gloss: The hall of residence on the hill's upper slope.

places.blurb: The hall of residence on the hill's upper slope: forty rooms around a courtyard, built from one shell, with each room's contents kept as data.

name.gloss: 'Upper tone' (an overtone); the Ueno stop.

places.blurb: The loop's stop under Jōon hill: a platform deep in the hill and an escalator climb to a pavilion in the park.

name.gloss: The shopping street under Jōon hill.

places.blurb: The covered shopping street under the hill, a torii tunnel up the steps, and Yoseatsume, the pawnshop of instruments and swords.

renders.caption: From the top of the steps

name.gloss: The Akiba stop and its streets.

places.blurb: Empty-Box Field, the electronics town: Denki-dōri under the viaduct, junk lanes of dead CRTs and a retro alley.

name.gloss: The guitar street and its station.

places.blurb: Tone-Deaf Water, the guitar street, where every shop has someone playing the same riff badly. The loop crosses the gorge on a bridge.

name.gloss: The central terminal, named after the city.

places.blurb: The central terminal, a labyrinth on four levels: fourteen exits, a bento street, an 18 m escalator climb, and 402 absurd signs.

name.gloss: The Shibuya crossing: every direction walks at once, under walls of giant screens.

places.blurb: Fave Valley's scramble crossing: every direction walks at once, under walls of giant screens.

name.gloss: The live-house district's station and streets.

places.blurb: Dues-Paying Marsh, the live-house district: a level crossing that never opens, the basement box NORMA, Honban Hall for the finale, and Tobiiri's Wednesday open mic.

name.gloss: The Sweets Town stop and its market street.

places.blurb: Sweets Town: a market street under the tracks, a chocolate auction called out by the box, Kurihara's bakery with a room to rent upstairs, and a food-crawl lane.

name.gloss: The busking park's station and gate.

places.blurb: Street-Live Park, the busking park: fourteen numbered pitches, a bridge everyone crosses, the cherry lawn under the skyline, a boating pond and an open-air stage.

name.gloss: Tuning Fork Tower: its crown is a tuning fork, tuned to A 440, and in typhoons it plays. The penthouse studio is on top.

places.blurb: Onsa Tower (音叉タワー), whose top floor is the penthouse studio, crowned with a tuning fork. At its foot: a covered passage from Onpuchō station through the lobby, an unmarked bronze door to the residence, 88 brass rods over the office lobby, and the Little Fork, a bronze tuning fork anyone may strike.

name.gloss: The tourist deck, 149 m up the lattice.

places.blurb: Onkyō Tower's main deck (音響タワー展望台), 149 m up the orange-and-white lattice: a glass box the tower's legs run straight through. Nineteen coin binoculars, each with a card of what it points at, a glass floor people lean beside rather than step on, Kyōmeidō's tuning-fork keyrings, Kissa Kōon's parfait on the mezzanine, and a radio booth that will play your request from the tower. Yes, you can see the school from here: bearing 298.

renders.caption: The glass floor, 149 m over the street

name.gloss: 'Upper tone' (an overtone); the Ueno stop. Home of 上音大, Jōon College of Music.
'Empty-Box Field': every collector keeps the box. The Akiba stop.
'In front of the Cat God', named the way real shrine stops are.
'Overtime Town'. The last train leaves full.
The cat-famous old town, spelled the way it sounds to its residents.
'Sweets Town': the market street under the tracks, one kana away from a real stop.
'Gold Seat': one metal up from Ginza, and priced accordingly.
The central terminal, named after the city. A labyrinth: fourteen exits, a bento street, and a platform ten minutes from anything.
'Noodle Refill'. The station is the second bowl.
'Harbour View'. Deadpan: platform-only stops get honest, dull names.
'Signature Song'. Everyone's, one room at a time.
'East Whatsitsname'. Nobody remembers.
'Sold Out'. The hub where limited editions go to vanish.
'Nothing'. One kanji, one bench, one vending machine.
'Ordinary', which is also the name of the stopping service: 'the Futsū for Futsū'.
'Fave Valley' (推し, oshi). Also the word for the staff who push commuters onto trains.
'Street-Live Park': buskers every metre.
'Bed Town', the loanword for a commuter suburb.
'Cat Teaser' (foxtail grass). The cats have a union.
'Late-Night Lodging': the city that never sleeps, one syllable from a real hub.
'Ladder', slang for hopping from bar to bar.
'Vending Hill', named like every suburb that isn't on a hill.
'Fish-Tank Bag': a one-kana shift, with an aquarium on the roof.
'Tone-Deaf Water': the guitar street, where every shop has someone playing the same riff badly.
'Dues-Paying Marsh' (下積み, the years unknown bands spend paying their dues).
'Metropolis'. Population about forty.
'West Again'.
'Fireworks Riverbank'.
'Factory Moe', which is a real hobby.
'The Stage': the island stop, one syllable off a real one.
'Sea Wall'. Deadpan.
'Squid Cove'.
'In front of Onkyō Tower'. Three lines meet here; 'meet at the tower' means four different exits.
'Note Town': used scores, used books, curry. Every shop smells of paper.
'Four-on-the-Floor' (四つ打ち): one letter off a real stop, and the club district.
'Cat Gate': a gate with a stone cat on it, older than the station. Nobody knows who put it there.
'Deficit Slope' (赤字, red ink): head offices, all downhill.
'Transfer'. A station with no exits: you can only change trains here.
'The Back Approach': vintage clothes, third-wave coffee, a queue outside every door.
'Staying Too Long': net cafés and all-night karaoke, where you end up after the last train.
The music college on Jōon hill.
The park on the hilltop around the campus.
The hall of residence on the hill's upper slope.
The shopping street under Jōon hill.
The Akiba stop and its streets.
The gorge of the Tone-Deaf Water.
The guitar street and its station.
The cat god's shrine on its hill.
The big city park of buskers and cherry trees.
The beach park on the island, with the outdoor stage on the shore.
The arena's plaza.
'Scale Slope': 音階 (a musical scale) with 階段 (stairs) inside it. Each step is a note; locals say it plays a major scale going down and a minor one coming up.
The refinery everyone comes to look at after dark.
The department store by the station, and the beer garden on its roof every summer.
The grassy levee (土手) on the river's north-east bank.

The orange-and-white lattice broadcast tower.
540 m, the tallest thing in the city. A cat tree is called a cat tower in Japanese, and this one got out of hand.
Lit in eight colours; locals argue about what the eighth one is.
Da capo: 'from the beginning'. It goes round, and you go back to the start. The top gondola is where people confess.
Where the concerts that matter happen, and then happen again.
Refineries on the shore lit up like a synth panel.

kit.name: CityKit
kit.does: plan.json in; terrain, rail, roads, parcels and every building out. Protected views keep the skyline composed; panoramas are rendered per viewpoint and time of day; the phone map on this page is its tile pyramid.

kit.name: Set-piece kit
kit.does: The streets and stations you walk: levels, walkable surfaces, crowd flow per time slot, busk sites, signs from a text atlas, shops as typed opportunities for the cast.

kit.name: Room kit
kit.does: Interiors from a room.json: walls, openings, finishes, lighting tiers, furniture kinds, and the city's panorama outside the window.

kit.name: StageKit
kit.does: Performance spaces from a preset: decks and risers, a lighting rig by channel with a DMX patch, PA, backline, marks and looks.
